user_need_match.quote: le else-if peut-il ecraser un etat legitime; y a-t-il d'autres chemins qui laissent .processing orphelin; coherence overlay/statusLine; changelogs identiques et valides
user_need_match.evidence: Q1: the else-if (AppDelegate.swift:2068-2074) is doubly guarded: .recording is unreachable there (early return via wasLatest at :2020/:2037) and the branch tests state == .processing explicitly; failSession is synchronous @MainActor with no suspension between the gate and the mutation. The flashInfo/flashError branches set state = .idle synchronously (:2432, :2459) BEFORE :2066, so the else-if never fires after a flash and overlay.hide() can never kill a visible flash. Q2: all 8 writers of state = .processing (:1907, :2067, :2174, :2196, :2221, :2308, :2329, :2905) were traced to a reset path (finish :2113 all branches, failSession post-fix, cancelEverything :1280 ending state = .idle at :1341); no other orphan path found. Q3: statusLine is only read under .processing (:2608, :2618-2621), quips stop at :2038, refreshUI fires via the state didSet (:42). Q4: changelog 0.9.110 byte-identical between app and site, tsc --noEmit exit 0, structural Swift checks pass.
edge_cases_covered: double silent failure with two inflight sessions (restore branch then step-down)
todo-capture success flash colliding with the step-down: unreachable interleaving (gates :624 and :329)
minimal overlay style (R10): overlay never shown, hide() is a no-op, the alert still appears
glass alert visible when the step-down fires: separate alertWindow (:3211), unaffected by overlay.hide()

findings.issue: The dictation state machine (state/inflight/overlay) has zero automated tests; the .processing latch shipped and was only caught by a user-visible dead key, and this fix lands with no regression test. The only suite is the Updater contract (70 tests, Linux-runnable).
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the failSession/finish state-transition decision into a pure, AppKit-free reducer and add a Linux-runnable contract test: silent failure with 0/1 remaining inflight sessions must yield .idle/.processing respectively.

findings.issue: Merge 9d75a20 is not pushed; the fix and the 0.9.110 changelog exist only locally (L0), and the live site does not show 0.9.110 until deploy.
findings.suggested_fix: Push main and deploy the website (out of scope for this read-only audit).

findings.issue: The latch release is silent: no VerbaLog line when the step-down fires, so a future recurrence of an orphaned .processing (or an unexpected step-down) leaves no trace, exactly like the original bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Log one line in the else-if branch (state stepped down .processing -> .idle, no inflight left).

The file is past the ~2000-line refactor alarm; the state machine's safety currently rests on whole-file manual reasoning (this audit is the evidence). Pre-existing.
The gather's 5 'high' oversized-file findings all point at .vercel/output build artifacts (minified bundles): falsified as out-of-scope, contribute zero to the score.

edge_cases.scenario: Two sessions inflight, both fail silent: first fail takes the restore branch (:2066-2067, hasInflight true), second takes the step-down (:2068-2074).
edge_cases.evidence_gathered: static trace of both passes through failSession; complete() removes each failed session before the test (SessionStore.swift:62)

edge_cases.scenario: Todo-capture success flash on screen when the last inflight session fails silent: overlay.hide() would cut the flash short, but the interleaving is unreachable (todo cannot start under .processing, gate :624; dictation cannot start during a todo capture, gate :329; idle+inflight is only ever transient within one synchronous MainActor run).

confidence_basis: Every static claim was directly verified by reading the cited lines and by 9 falsifiable tests (all listed with actual outputs); the changelog half has runtime evidence (tsc exit 0). Confidence stays medium, not high, for one honest reason: the Swift app cannot be built or run on this Linux box (Package.swift gates the app target behind #if os(macOS)), so the fix's behavior was never observed at runtime; a macOS build + a manual silent-dictation repro (mute input, dictate, then press the transform key) remains the missing L1 evidence.
